meta.name: Review and Approval Workspace
meta.description: Focused review layout for evaluating evidence and a machine-generated or third-party proposal, then capturing an explicit, justified, auditable human decision.

purpose: Let an eligible reviewer inspect the original evidence, understand a proposed recommendation with its provenance and confidence, and record a deliberate, justified, auditable decision without ever presenting the recommendation itself as an already-made decision.
useWhen: A machine-generated, third-party, or delegated proposal requires human review before it takes effect.
The action being reviewed is a decision, approval, rejection, or conflict resolution with durable consequences.
The evidence behind the proposal must remain inspectable and separate from the proposal's conclusion.
The decision must be recorded with actor, timestamp, and justification for later audit.
doNotUseWhen: The screen only displays a read-only record with no pending decision.
The action is a routine, low-consequence toggle that does not require justification or audit.
No evidence or recommendation exists yet to review — use the entity-detail recipe instead.
The route performs authentication, verification, or account recovery — use the authentication recipe.
requiredInputs: Approved evidence-rendering components for the domain's document/source types
Justification requirements for approval, rejection, and conflict resolution
Guard/eligibility checklist for the reviewed action

selectionQuestions: What is the exact object/version being reviewed, and does the evidence shown resolve to that exact object?
Who produced the proposal (machine, third party, delegate) and what is its confidence/provenance?
What guard checks must pass before the primary decision action is eligible?
What must the reviewer record when approving, rejecting, or resolving a conflict (actor, justification, alternative preserved)?
What happens to the evidence and proposal if either becomes stale before the decision is submitted?
Is the reviewer's role eligible to decide, or only to view?

regions.name: Review Header
regions.role: Identify the exact object under review, its current status, the dominant pending decision, and the eligible reviewer context.
prohibitedComponents: Primary decision action placed only here without also appearing in decisionForm
Ambiguous status text without a structured state

compact.notes: Status must remain legible; never truncate the pending-decision label.

medium.layout: Identity and status on one line, breadcrumb above.

wide.layout: Identity, status, and context in one row.
wide.notes: Do not compress the status indicator into an icon-only badge.

ultrawide.layout: Identity, status, and context in one row.
ultrawide.notes: Keep the header height stable regardless of viewport width.

rules: The reviewed object's exact identifier and version are always visible.
Status uses a structured state, never a free-text-only label.
Status shown here must match the status shown in any list view of the same object (single canonical source).

regions.name: Evidence Viewer
regions.role: Render the original, immutable source evidence (document, excerpt, message, or record) that the proposal is based on.
prohibitedComponents: Evidence rendered from a broader/consolidated aggregate instead of the exact cited record

scroll.notes: Long evidence scrolls independently without capturing the page's primary vertical scroll.

regions.visibilityCondition: Always visible when evidence exists; a structured empty/unavailable state otherwise.

compact.layout: Full-width evidence panel, collapsible if long.
compact.notes: Never require horizontal scroll to read evidence text.

medium.placement: Below the review header, above the proposal.

wide.placement: Left column of a two-column review layout.
wide.layout: Constrained evidence panel beside the proposal and decision form.
wide.notes: Evidence and decisionForm never share one scroll container.

ultrawide.placement: Left column of a two-column review layout.
ultrawide.notes: Do not stretch evidence width beyond a readable measure.

rules: Evidence renders exactly the cited record/excerpt, resolved via one canonical resolver, never a guessed or partial match.
The evidence source remains visually and structurally separate from the proposal's interpretation of it.
The original evidence is never mutated by review actions; corrections are captured as new linked records.

regions.name: Evidence Navigator
regions.role: Move between multiple cited evidence items or excerpts belonging to the same review without leaving the page.
prohibitedComponents: Navigation entries with no resolvable target
Dead '#' links standing in for an unbuilt route
regions.visibilityCondition: Visible only when more than one evidence item is cited.

compact.notes: Keep touch targets at the approved minimum size.

medium.notes: Wrap rather than truncate evidence labels.

wide.notes: Keep the active evidence item clearly indicated.

ultrawide.notes: Do not add more than the cited evidence items.

rules: Every navigator entry resolves to a real evidence item; an entity referenced without a built route opens a resolver-backed overlay, never a dead link.
The active evidence item is programmatically indicated, not color-only.

regions.name: Critical Review Context
regions.role: Surface guard checks, blocking dependencies, missing data, and eligibility state that determine whether the primary decision action is currently available.
prohibitedComponents: Conflating a normal dependency with a business blocker
Confidence-qualifier prefixes on a confirmed operational state
regions.visibilityCondition: Always visible; shows a clear 'no blocking condition' state when every guard passes.

compact.notes: Every guard item remains individually readable.

medium.notes: Do not collapse guard items into a single summary line.

wide.notes: Each guard item shows its own pass/fail state.

ultrawide.notes: Preserve one guard item per line.

rules: Each guard/eligibility item is classified as exactly one of: execution status, human-pending, dependency, business blocker, permission, or technical error — never a combined free-text label.
A dependency that the primary decision action itself will resolve is never classified as a business blocker of that same action.
The primary decision action is disabled, with a visible reason, whenever any blocking guard fails.

regions.name: Proposal and Recommendation
regions.role: Present the machine-generated, third-party, or delegated recommendation with its confidence and provenance, clearly separated from the evidence and from the final decision.
prohibitedComponents: Presenting the recommendation as an already-made decision
Confidence rendered as 0 when no canonical value exists
regions.visibilityCondition: Always visible when a recommendation exists; a structured empty state otherwise.

compact.layout: Stacked recommendation summary with confidence and provenance.
compact.notes: Confidence and provenance remain visible, not hidden behind a tooltip.

wide.placement: Right column, below the critical review context.
wide.notes: Keep recommendation visually distinct from the decision form below it.

ultrawide.placement: Right column, below the critical review context.
ultrawide.notes: Do not widen beyond a readable measure.

rules: Confidence is a number or explicitly null; null means no canonical value exists and is never rendered as zero.
Every claim traces to a resolvable source reference in the evidence viewer.
The recommendation never carries an approval or rejection control of its own; only the decision form does.

regions.name: Decision Form
regions.role: Capture the reviewer's explicit decision, required justification, and, for a conflict, the preserved rejected alternative.
prohibitedComponents: Submitting without a required justification when the recipe's decision policy requires one
A decision control duplicated outside this region
Silent discard of a rejected alternative during conflict resolution
regions.visibilityCondition: Always visible; disabled with a visible reason when a guard in criticalReviewContext fails or eligibility is absent.

compact.notes: The primary decision action remains full width and reachable without scrolling past unrelated content.

wide.notes: Keep the decision panel fixed relative to evidence scrolling on tall pages.

ultrawide.notes: Do not widen the justification field beyond a readable measure.

rules: Every decision records actor, timestamp, justification, and result before it takes effect.
A conflict resolution preserves the rejected alternative in the audit trail; it is never silently discarded.
The decision action re-validates every guard immediately before applying, never trusting a UI-computed eligibility flag alone.
A pending submission disables the decision action to prevent duplicate decisions.

regions.name: Audit Context
regions.role: Show the history of prior decisions, guard evaluations, and state transitions for this object, each with a correlation id linking related changes.
prohibitedComponents: History entries without actor and timestamp

scroll.notes: A long history scrolls independently of the main review flow.

regions.visibilityCondition: Visible when at least one prior decision or transition exists.

compact.notes: Collapse by default to keep the decision form reachable first.

wide.placement: Full width below the two-column review area.
wide.notes: Independent scroll region, never the page's only scroll owner.

ultrawide.placement: Full width below the two-column review area.
ultrawide.notes: Keep entries in strict chronological order.

rules: Every entry links related objects through the same correlation id used by the decision that produced it.
A rejected alternative from a conflict resolution remains visible here, never removed.

composition.columnPolicy: Single stacked column on compact and medium layouts; two-column split (evidence left, guard/proposal/decision right) on wide and ultrawide layouts.
spacingOwnership: The layout owns spacing between the header, evidence column, and decision column.
The evidence viewer owns spacing between the source content and its own scroll edges.
The decision form owns spacing between fields, justification, and the primary action.
surfacePolicy: The evidence viewer uses one clear surface, distinct from the proposal panel.
Critical review context uses the critical surface treatment.
The proposal panel never reuses the decision form's surface, so recommendation and decision remain visually distinguishable.
composition.scrollOwner: browser document, with the evidence viewer and audit context as independent region-scoped scroll containers
rules: Evidence, recommendation, and decision remain three visually distinct regions at every breakpoint.
The primary decision action is reachable without requiring the reviewer to scroll past the full audit history.
No nested application shell duplicates chrome already provided by the page shell.
prohibited: Merging evidence and recommendation into a single unstructured block.
A decision control rendered outside decisionForm.
Two independent full-height vertical scroll containers competing for the same viewport.
Color as the only distinguishing signal between guard-pass and guard-fail states.

actions.primaryPlacement: Inside the decision form, after justification and any required conflict-resolution input.
actions.secondaryPlacement: Request more evidence, defer, or delegate — placed beside the primary action with lower visual weight.
actions.destructivePlacement: Rejection uses a distinct, explicitly confirmed control inside the decision form; it is not merged with approval.
actions.bulkPlacement: Not applicable — this recipe reviews one object at a time.
actions.contextualPlacement: Guard-specific resolution actions (e.g. resolve a missing dependency) appear inside criticalReviewContext, next to the guard they resolve.
actions.overflowPolicy: Rare secondary actions may move to an accessible overflow menu; the primary decision action never moves there.
actions.compactBehavior: The primary decision action becomes full width and remains pinned above the fold once all guards pass.
rules: Exactly one primary decision action is dominant per state.
Approval, rejection, and conflict resolution are distinct controls, never one control with a mode switch.
The primary action stays disabled, with a visible reason, until every blocking guard passes.
A pending decision prevents duplicate submission.

content.headingPolicy: One h1 identifies the object under review; evidence, proposal, and decision each use their own subsection heading at a consistent level.
content.longContentPolicy: Evidence excerpts, justification text, and audit entries expand within their own scroll region without widening the page.
content.truncationPolicy: Never truncate evidence text, guard reasons, justification, or audit before/after values.
content.emptyStatePlacement: A missing recommendation or absent evidence renders a dedicated, honest empty state in its own region, never a silently blank panel.
content.loadingStrategy: Evidence, proposal, and audit context each show their own skeleton; the decision form remains disabled until its dependencies resolve.
content.errorScope: A failure loading evidence or the proposal is scoped to its own region; it does not collapse the whole review page.
rules: Status, severity, and guard labels use the same vocabulary and computation as any list view of the same object.
Confidence-qualifier language (e.g. a 'candidate' prefix) is used only for genuinely unconfirmed inference, never for a confirmed operational state.
Messages describing the current state and next available action; no leftover internal planning language.

responsive.primaryViewport: Desktop review workstations and tablet-class review on the go.
responsive.zoomExpectation: The review flow must remain usable at 200% zoom where practical and at minimum 125% browser zoom.
responsive.internalOverflowPolicy: The evidence viewer and audit context scroll independently; the page itself scrolls vertically as the sole document-level scroll owner.

transformations.change: Keep the two-column split but narrow both columns proportionally.
transformations.reason: Evidence and decision remain readable without unnecessary whitespace.

transformations.change: Collapse the two-column split into a single stacked column: evidence, guard context, proposal, decision, audit.
transformations.reason: A narrower viewport cannot sustain a readable two-column review.

transformations.change: Stack every region full width; collapse audit context by default; keep the primary decision action reachable without excessive scrolling.
transformations.reason: Compact viewports require a single clear path from evidence to decision.

states.rendering: Show skeletons for header, evidence, proposal, and decision form without a premature guard result.
Render evidence, guard context, proposal, and an eligible or ineligible decision form.
states.userAction: Review the evidence and proposal, then decide.

states.rendering: Render whichever of evidence, proposal, or audit context is available; the missing part shows its own honest empty state and, if it blocks the decision, appears in criticalReviewContext.
states.userAction: Continue with what is available or wait for the missing part.

states.rendering: Communicate a non-blocking concern (e.g. evidence updated since last view) without disabling the decision.
states.userAction: Acknowledge and continue, or refresh evidence first.

states.rendering: Render a safe, region-scoped error for evidence, proposal, or submission failure; never a raw transport error.
Render evidence and proposal as read-only when the current role is not eligible to decide, with a visible reason.
states.userAction: Request delegation or escalate to an eligible reviewer.

states.rendering: Disable the decision form and show a pending indicator while the decision is being recorded.
Explain that the evidence or proposal changed since it was loaded and require a refresh before the decision action re-enables.
states.userAction: Refresh evidence and proposal before deciding.

landmarkMap: The evidence viewer and decision form use distinct landmarks so a screen-reader user can jump directly between them.
Critical review context uses section semantics with an accessible name describing its guard-checklist role.
Audit context uses a section landmark distinct from the main review flow.
headingStructure: One h1 identifies the object under review.
Evidence, proposal, decision, and audit each introduce their own heading at a consistent sublevel.
keyboard: Evidence navigation, guard-resolution actions, and the decision form are fully keyboard operable.
An overlay opened from an unresolved-route citation returns focus to its exact triggering element on close.
Focus moves to the first invalid field or the error summary after a rejected submission.
announcements: A guard becoming eligible or blocking is perceivable, not only a color change.
Successful decision submission and its result are announced.
The stale state is announced when evidence or proposal changes after load.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Guard pass/fail, confidence, and decision result never depend on color alone.
rules: Every guard item has an accessible name describing what it checks and its current result.
The primary decision action's disabled reason is exposed to assistive technology, not only shown visually.

prohibitedPatterns: Presenting a recommendation as a final decision.
Submitting a decision against evidence known to be stale.
A dependency the action itself resolves classified as a blocker of that action.
Silently discarding a rejected alternative during conflict resolution.
A citation to an entity without a built route rendered as a dead link instead of a resolver-backed overlay.
dataMagnitude: Evidence excerpts and justification text may expand substantially through localization or verbose source content.
Audit history may grow unbounded over the object's lifetime and must remain independently scrollable.
performance: Do not block rendering of evidence and proposal on the full audit history loading.
Guard re-validation before submission must complete before the decision action's pending state resolves.
Avoid recomputing guard eligibility independently in more than one place; reuse one shared guard function.
implementation: Guard checks are itemized and evaluated by one shared, pure function reused by every consumer (list row, this page, the submission handler).
The decision handler re-runs every guard immediately before mutating, never trusting a UI-computed flag alone.
Every decision produces a durable audit entry with actor, timestamp, justification, result, and a correlation id linking every touched object.
The original evidence record is never mutated; corrections are captured as new linked records.
Machine presence conditions come from presenceDefaults; visibilityCondition prose is explanatory only.

presenceDefaults.rationale: Every review requires exact object/version orientation and current decision context.
The evidence region remains structural even when evidence is unavailable so the absence is rendered honestly instead of silently collapsing.
Navigation exists only when the reviewer can actually choose between multiple cited evidence items.
Guard context always renders, including the explicit no-blocking-condition state when every guard passes.
The proposal region remains structural so a missing or unavailable recommendation is represented by an explicit state rather than disappearing.
The decision region remains visible even when ineligible; guard or permission state disables it with a visible reason.
Prior-decision history appears only when at least one auditable transition exists.

checks.description: The review-approval recipe must validate against the layout recipe schema.
checks.remediation: Correct invalid or missing recipe fields.

checks.description: The decision form's primary action must remain disabled, with a visible and accessible reason, whenever a guard in criticalReviewContext fails.
checks.remediation: Correct guard evaluation wiring between criticalReviewContext and decisionForm.

checks.description: The recommendation in proposalAndRecommendation must never be presented as an already-made decision, and confidence must render as null (not zero) when no canonical value exists.
checks.remediation: Correct recommendation copy and confidence rendering.

checks.description: Every submitted decision must produce an audit entry with actor, timestamp, justification, result, and correlation id before the action's success state renders.
checks.remediation: Correct the decision handler's audit-trail write path.

checks.description: The two-column evidence/decision split must collapse to a single stacked column without horizontal overflow at compact and medium viewports.
checks.remediation: Correct responsive transformation and container width.

checks.description: Review evidence, recommendation, decision, navigator, and audit regions must follow typed recipe presence semantics while honest missing-data states remain structurally visible.
checks.remediation: Correct craftDefaults/presenceDefaults and keep conditional regions required=false with cardinality.minimum=0.

examples.name: Approve a machine-generated deadline recommendation
examples.description: Evidence document, deadline calculation with confidence and trace, guard checklist confirming role eligibility, and a decision form requiring justification before confirming the deadline.

examples.name: Resolve a scheduling conflict between two candidate dates
examples.description: Two candidate evidence sources side by side via the evidence navigator, a recommendation favoring one, and a decision form that records the choice and preserves the rejected alternative in the audit trail.
